$comment: Ceiling for scripts/check-repetition.mjs. A change may not raise it. When a change LOWERS the count, run `node scripts/check-repetition.mjs --update` and commit — the ceiling ratchets down and cannot drift back up. The goal is not zero: a deliberate callback is repetition on purpose.
$raise: 7 → 8 in site#233 §3, the one raise this file records, and it is against the rule above. Stated plainly rather than absorbed: the claims registry on /conformance publishes each claim's CANONICAL sentence, and blog/bifurcation-and-inter-contract-enforcement.md legitimately discusses those same claims. The residual is ONE blog sentence — 'So docs generate from source and fail CI on drift, and behaviour specs execute against the engine' — which is compound, so it now matches c1's and c2's atomic canonical sentences as TWO pairs (56% and 40%) where it previously matched one compound homepage paraphrase as ONE (50%). Net +1. Neither side is deletable: the registry must quote the graph verbatim or it is not a registry, and rewording a published essay to satisfy a vocabulary-overlap heuristic is the 'fighting the voice' failure docs/evidence-edges.md names as the sign that the predicate is wrong. The same change REMOVED three larger restatements (83%/50%/36%) by deleting the homepage's drifted paraphrases of c1/c5/c6 — the drift issue 233 §3 reported — so the page says the same thing fewer times than before at every threshold that matters. check-repetition has no per-pair exemption mechanism; one was NOT invented for this.
$note: scripts/check-repetition.mjs --update rewrites this file with a hardcoded $comment and drops every other key, so the two fields above do not survive the next ratchet. Re-add them, or move this rationale into the script, if the ceiling moves again.
